subject: Tenancy namespace mapping and ops contract draft
messages:
From: Laura Newman <laura.newman@edgeworks.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: EdgeWorks Procurement <procurement@edgeworks.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Tenancy namespace mapping questions for private VPC deploy

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the performance numbers looked promising. Before we finalize the purchase order, our network/security team needs clarity about how Redwood will map tenant namespaces to our on-prem racks and what control-plane responsibilities remain on EdgeWorks vs Redwood in the private VPC model. Specific asks: 

1) A concise diagram that shows namespace -> subnet mapping and where the Redwood control plane sits relative to our management VLANs.
2) Who owns cert rotation for control-plane endpoints?
3) Recommended ops responsibilities for tenant onboarding and emergency access (SRE runbooks).

Can you share a short reference doc and any runbook links we can circulate internally?

Also, procurement asked for a short ops SLA matrix for support windows tied to our reserved capacity purchase.

Best,
Laura
Laura Newman
Head of Platform Engineering, EdgeWorks Systems
[Attachment: edgeworks-internal-network.pdf (referenced)]

From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Laura Newman <laura.newman@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenancy namespace mapping questions for private VPC deploy

Laura — thanks for the clear asks. Attaching a lightweight reference diagram and an ops SLA draft to answer each point. High level answers first: 

• Namespace -> Subnet mapping: we recommend one isolated namespace per tenant mapped to a dedicated subnet (example in attached diagram). Control-plane traffic (control API, telemetry, and auth) uses a separate management subnet with peering to tenant subnets via your edge router.

• Cert rotation: Redwood can operate control-plane cert rotation as an opt-in managed service (we hold the certs and rotate per agreed policy) or we provide automation and a key-rotation runbook if you prefer to manage keys in your KMS. For regulated environments, customers typically host keys in their own HSM; in that mode we push rotated certs and you approve via an automation webhook.

• Ops responsibilities: see the attached checklist. Short summary: Redwood handles model-serving runtime upgrades, KV cache integrity, and autoscaling policies. EdgeWorks owns physical network ACLs, tenant VLAN assignment, and cross-tenant firewall rules. We propose a joint on-call rota for the first 90 days.

Next steps I propose: Jonas to drive a one-hour architecture walk with your network team next week and Marissa will align the runbook acceptance criteria. If that works, I'll circulate calendar invites and a short pre-read.

Attachments:
- namespace-mapping-v1.svg (diagram)
- ops-sla-matrix.xlsx (draft)

Cheers,
Mateo
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: namespace-mapping-v1.svg (diagram)]
[Attachment: ops-sla-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Newman <laura.newman@edgeworks.com>
Date: 2026-10-13T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tenancy namespace mapping questions for private VPC deploy

Thanks — skimming Mateo's attachments. Couple of convo items to drive during the arc-walk: 

1) Delegation model: propose we define three delegation levels in the runbook: "Edge-only" (customer manages all keys and certs), "Shared" (Redwood rotates certs with your KMS handshake), "Fully-managed" (Redwood holds certs, rotation SLA). We'll map each level to acceptance tests.

2) Network demarc: your team asked about hairpin NAT for control-plane telemetry. We should validate whether EdgeWorks prefers telemetry over a peered mgmt subnet vs TLS ingest back to Redwood-hosted endpoints — both are supported but have different failure modes.

3) Can Marissa pull the current runbook link and add the onboarding checklist items we discussed (IP allocation, ACL templates, example cert webhook payload)? I've added a short draft checklist below.

— Draft checklist (for discussion):
- Confirm tenant namespace name and labels
- Allocate /26 subnet (suggested default) and reserve first .4 for control proxies
- ACL template applied (deny all inbound except health probes)
- Cert rotation mode selected + KMS thumbprint recorded
- Emergency admin SSH/console access window documented

I'll seed the arc-walk agenda once we have your preferred times.

— Jonas
Principal Network Architect, Redwood Inference
